newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia profit helped by strong mobile phones.
newsitem.headline: Nokia profit helped by strong mobile phones.

text.p: Finnish telecommunications group Nokia Oy on Thursday said 58 percent growth in mobile phone sales helped bring nine-month pre-tax earnings to 2.2 billion markka, matching analysts' expectations.

Nokia said January-September profit before tax and minorities was 2.23 billion down from 3.98 billion in the same period last year, and the company said it was maintaining its generally favourable outlook for the rest of the year.
"For the rest of the year we maintain our generally positive outlook," Nokia said in its interim report.
"We are especially pleased with the high growth in sales and progress in achieving operating efficiencies within Nokia Mobile Phones," Nokia CEO Jorma Ollila said in the statement.
Third-quarter mobile phone net sales increased 58 percent, while third-quarter sales of telecommunications systems, Nokia's other mainstay business, increased 26 percent.
Group net sales rose to 26.65 billion markka from 25.86 billion in the year-ago period.
Nokia attributed the strong performance in mobile phones to continued buoyant demand in Europe and Asia, as well as to the recent introduction of new products.
While the rate of growth in telecommunications sales fell short of Nokia's expectations, earnings by the division were higher than Nokia had envisaged.
"Although sales of the (telecommunications) business group grew at a somewhat slower rate than expected, profits exceeded our expectations," Ollila said.
Nokia's profit was in line with analysts' forecasts at 2.2 billion markka in a 2.0-2.4 billion range.
The result corresponded to earnings per share of 5.70 markka, down from 10.50 markka a year earlier.
On the Helsinki Stock Exchange, Nokia jumped on the news of the result, rising 13.00 markka to a 12-month high 240.00 before easing to 238.00.
